name: King of Hormah
overview: The King of Hormah was a male ruler who is known primarily for being one of thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua in the conquest of Canaan. His tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. This king represents one of the many local rulers subdued during Israel's divinely sanctioned campaign under Joshua's leadership.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Hormah' is straightforward, indicating his rulership over the city of Hormah. The name itself simply identifies his position without additional symbolic meaning. It is recorded in Joshua 12:14 as a title rather than a personal name given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Hormah beyond his identification as a defeated king in Joshua 12:14. There are no listed relatives or alliances noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Hormah is significant in the biblical narrative as a representative of the Canaanite resistance against Israel's entrance into the Promised Land. His defeat by Joshua underscores God's faithfulness in granting Israel victory over its enemies, fulfilling His promises to His people. This king's inclusion among those conquered highlights the comprehensive nature of Israel's conquest under divine guidance.
